body:
I'm being slightly defensive here by returning (total - 1) instead of the full thread count. While the sample in #104428 doesn't freeze with the full pool size, in my actual project it consistently hangs unless one thread is reserved.

I need to test on a low end device with `cpus < pthread (8)`, and maybe add `navigator.hardwareConcurrency - 1` to the mix. Or maybe that logic should be done in `OS_Web::get_default_thread_pool_size()`

> in my actual project it consistently hangs unless one thread is reserved.

You mean without doing `Math.max(1, total - 1)`?
I agree, I was being a bit more defensive than usual since wasn't sure in which emscripten version it was added.
Oh, didn't think about that. Mmmm. I'll investigate.

https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/blame/62d4b1cc0b98d2a2ccdd59e0fc24d76703e1d866/src/lib/libpthread.js#L79-L81

I think we're OK! :)
Correct, didn't investigate any further being honest.

cc @Faless. Can you confirm that this avoids the problem you identified in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/54499 It seems like we are querying the number of web workers allocated by emscriptem rather than just querying the number of processors. That sounds like the right solution to me, but I am not well versed in Javascript/emscriptem.

Bottom line, we can't use only one thread in the WTP. We generally need at least 3 (in the case the separate rendering thread and separate physics thread are enabled.

I comment about this [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104458#discussion_r2008222268), but I'm still unsure since the actual thread pool is hardcoded to 8 even if the user has less processors.

What we can do though is change `-sPTHREAD_POOL_SIZE=8` to something like:

```
-sPTHREAD_POOL_SIZE=Math.max(3, Math.min(8, navigator.hardwareConcurrency))
```

See: https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/blob/36423eb7efbecfb901300dd65d3f06967fafd984/src/settings.js#L1667-L1675

To me, that seems like a safe and logical option.

My only concern is @Faless' comment:

> We can likely improve the whole ThreadPoolWork in the future to always allocate X amount of threads, and assign jobs to them on the fly, but that will require some more architectural changes.

It makes me think that there is some fundamental limitation with the browser that makes this a challenge, rather than the problem just being that we didn't request emscriptem to pre-allocate enough threads

@clayjohn pushed with

```
-sPTHREAD_POOL_SIZE=Math.min(8,navigator.hardwareConcurrency)
```
Which results in the following emscripten code:
```js
var pthreadPoolSize=Math.min(8,navigator.hardwareConcurrency)
```

I removed the `Math.max(3,...)`  because if the user does not have 3 cores, then it doesn't matter whether the threadpool size is 3 or 1 . If the minimum required for multithreading is 3, the engine should fallback to single threaded, but I think that's outside of the scope of this PR (not sure whether that logic is implemented already)

body:
Something like "Override for the default size of the WorkerThreadPool. This setting is used when the WorkerThreadPool size is set to -1 (which it is by default). This size must be smaller than [member variant/emscripten_pool_size] otherwise deadlocks may occur. When using threads this size needs to be large enough to accommodate features that rely on having a dedicated thread like [member ProjectSettings.physics/2d/run_on_separate_thread] or [member ProjectSettings.rendering/driver/threads/thread_model]. In general, it is best to ensure that this is at least 4 and is at least at least 2 or three less than [member variant/emscripten_pool_size]."

@Faless How does that sound?
